page: Amazon Web Services c6id.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local NVMe SSD storage is bundled, providing 474 GB of instance store capacity. The baseline network bandwidth is rated at 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the c6id.2xlarge in the average performance tier for most compute and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded scores of 1894.18 and 7735.64, respectively, while the Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores reached 1610.0 and 6004.0. Memory bandwidth tests showed 413.67 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 58.2 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, certain workloads show performance limitations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scored 31.82 GB/sec, which is categorized as weak, and Redis SET operations achieved 7.96 million operations per second, also in the weak tier. Large-model LLM inference is highly constrained, with the 7B model prompt processing dropping to a poor 16.29 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c6id.2xlarge offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring dedicated compute power alongside high-speed local NVMe storage. The inclusion of 474 GB of local NVMe SSD storage reduces the need for external block storage for temporary data, optimizing the overall resource-to-cost ratio for specific tasks. This hardware profile is suitable for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, image processing, and database operations that benefit from local scratch space. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale language model inference due to its 16 GB memory limit and weak multi-threaded decompression and Redis performance.
description: Amazon Web Services c6id.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance powered by an 8-vCPU Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. It features 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory and a bundled 474 GB local NVMe SSD instance store. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance delivers average performance across standard compute benchmarks, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 6004.0 and a static web serving throughput of 12.34 GB/sec. However, it exhibits performance trade-offs, with weak results in Redis SET operations and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, alongside poor prompt processing speeds for 7B LLM models. The c6id.2xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring dedicated CPU cores paired with fast local scratch storage, making it suitable for software compilation, image processing, and web serving, while remaining constrained for memory-heavy or large-scale inference tasks.
